metadata.title: Expectancy-value profiles in math: How are student-perceived teaching behaviors related to motivational transitions?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses German participation in PISA 2012 and its national extension PISA Plus 2012–2013, with a longitudinal subsample followed from Grade 9 (t1, 2012) to Grade 10 (t2, 2013). Because the longitudinal sample at t2 is reduced by both curricular non-coverage of Grade 10 and voluntary follow-up participation, the authors rely on sampling-failure adjusted design weights that are available in the dataset to compensate for biases in representativeness of the remaining longitudinal students. In the subsequent analyses, these sampling-failure adjusted weights are explicitly included in the Mplus multinomial logistic regression models via the Mplus “weight” option. For the person-centered latent profile/transition analyses, the paper reports weighted parameters for descriptive statistics and uses the imputed datasets for the LTA three-step procedure, but it does not provide a specific weight variable name in the excerpt.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Data come from Germany’s PISA 2012 mathematics assessment and the national extension PISA Plus 2012–2013, with motivational constructs measured in Grades 9 (t1) and 10 (t2). The authors start from a longitudinal baseline sample of n=4610 students with both measurement time points, then restrict to a subsample of n=2605 students from 198 classrooms in 121 schools. The key selection criterion is that the mathematics teacher does not change between Grade 9 and Grade 10, to keep teaching quality comparable across time. The longitudinal sample is further constrained by the PISA Plus design: students without a Grade 10 level provided for curricular reasons are excluded, and voluntary follow-up at t2 leads to additional dropout. For missing questionnaire data, the authors use multiple imputation (m=20) with auxiliary variables from the common questionnaire part; for motivational constructs and teaching-behavior measures, only students with the relevant rotated-design coverage at Grade 9 and Grade 10 are included in the imputation/analysis workflow.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2012 (Germany) Grade 9–10 Mathematics; PISA Plus 2012–2013 longitudinal motivational profiles
main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent profile analysis selected a 3-profile solution at Grade 9 (entropy indicates high classification quality; average latent class probabilities p=.81–.88). Between-profile differences in motivational variables were highly significant (MANOVA reported in Appendix E; all pairwise comparisons p<.001). Profile sizes: Disengaged 20.9% (n=545), Highly motivated 24.7% (n=646), Confident but more or less engaged 54.3% (n=1414).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2012 (Germany) Grade 9–10 Mathematics data from PISA Plus 2012–2013, the study leveraged student gender, perceived teaching behaviors, and achievement-related variables to characterize motivational profile membership at Grade 9, finding that three distinct expectancy-value/self-efficacy profiles emerged with high classification quality (average latent class probabilities p=.81–.88) and large profile size differences. This indicates that German lower-secondary students’ motivation in mathematics is not uniform but clusters into qualitatively different patterns, suggesting that classroom interventions should be tailored to students’ motivational profile rather than relying on one-size-fits-all support.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2012 (Germany) Grade 9–10 Mathematics; PISA Plus 2012–2013 longitudinal motivational transitions
main_findings.target_variable: Motivational transitions from Grade 9 to Grade 10 latent profiles
main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent transition analysis with partial structural similarity; transition probabilities in the final model ranged from p=.832 to p=.845 (high classification quality). Stability: within-profile persistence was high (e.g., Confident but more or less engaged: 83.2% remained; Highly motivated: 83.5% remained; Disengaged: 84.5% remained). Teaching-behavior effects on transitions (reference class: Highly motivated): teacher support reduced odds of being in Disengaged at Grade 9 (OR=0.30, p<.001) and reduced odds of being in Confident but more or less engaged at Grade 9 (OR=0.52, p<.001), but did not affect transitions; student-oriented teaching predicted motivational change, reducing odds of transitioning to Confident but more or less engaged instead of Highly motivated at Grade 10 (OR=0.43, p=.005).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2012 (Germany) Grade 9–10 Mathematics data from PISA Plus 2012–2013, the study leveraged perceived teacher support and student-oriented teaching to predict motivational transitions between latent profiles, finding that profile membership was largely stable across time (transition probabilities p=.832–.845; within-profile stability ~83–85%) and that student-oriented teaching—more than general teacher support—was associated with more adaptive motivational change (OR=0.43, p=.005). This indicates that instructional practices that directly orient learning to students’ needs can help prevent declines into less adaptive motivation patterns during adolescence, although the study is observational and cannot establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes Germany’s PISA 2012 mathematics assessment and the national longitudinal extension PISA Plus 2012–2013, focusing on Grade 9 (t1, 2012) to Grade 10 (t2, 2013) motivational belief profiles. The analytic sample is n=2605 students in 198 classrooms across 121 schools, selected to keep the mathematics teacher constant from Grade 9 to Grade 10. Motivational constructs (self-efficacy, interest, utility value) are used to form three latent profiles at Grade 9, with high classification quality (average latent class probabilities p=.81–.88) and clear profile sizes (20.9%, 24.7%, 54.3%). Latent transition analysis shows strong stability across time (transition probabilities p=.832–.845; within-profile persistence ~83–85%). Perceived student-oriented teaching in Grade 9 is linked to more adaptive motivational transitions (OR=0.43, p=.005), while general teacher support does not affect transitions. Limitations include person-centered modeling rather than predictive ML, observational design, and reliance on multiple imputation for missing questionnaire data.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is not an empirical predictive ML study: it uses latent profile analysis and latent transition analysis (person-centered mixture modeling) with multinomial logistic regression and three-step LTA procedures in Mplus. Therefore, no supervised machine-learning algorithms are trained or compared, and the ml_techniques section is intentionally empty. The extraction focuses on the person-centered statistical results rather than ML performance metrics.
